FOUND s501b (Opus, 2026-09-30) by the breaking-case probe for #2285.  PRE-EXISTING (base 1bae682b gives the same wrong answer).  SILENT WRONG.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s501b/p/ev2.pl row 3 in the s501b worktree):
    our $o = "main-o"; $Foo::o = "foo-o";
    my $r3 = eval 'sub { package Foo; $o }'; print $r3->(), "\n";
perl: main-o  (an `our` is a LEXICALLY scoped alias; the eval's text is compiled in the caller's scope, so $o is main's)
PCL:  foo-o

CAUSE: #2285 (s501b) made a name in the eval's CAPTURE ALIST bind as a lexical in the package-switch requalifier (_binding_at's eval-mode tail).  An `our` alias is not in the capture alist (the alist carries my/state containers), so the requalifier's four-way resolver answers "(d) global of X" and rewrites $o to $Foo::o.  The eval site would have to hand the compiler its in-scope `our` aliases (name -> declaring package), the way it hands the capture names and the feature list (#364), and _binding_at would answer that package for them (its (a)-our arm).  The same missing fact probably breaks `our $o; eval '$o'` inside a `package Other;` section of the CALLER -- measure that first (cheap: one line each way).

BAR: Pl/ => corpus-diff + the eval cache key must include whatever new input the compiler reads (the s387 rule); guard rows in Pl/t/eval-capture-01.t.

=== s543c (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21, CODE 64353611 -- after s543b's eval-capture change) ===
VERDICT: LIVE -- as filed, and the plain spelling too (silent):
    our $o = "main-o"; $Foo::o = "foo-o"; my $r3 = eval 'sub { package Foo; $o }'; print $r3->();   perl main-o   PCL foo-o
    my $r4 = eval 'package Foo; $o';                                                              perl main-o   PCL foo-o
LABEL: silent (subject now says so).


=== DONE (s543h) ===
Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22, WIP f8cb0fad (batch HEAD 3b030913).  MEASURED: `eval 'package Foo; $o'` compiled `$o` as a p-eval-thunk
parameter looked up in Foo (the region binding); `eval 'sub { package Foo; $o }'` was requalified to `$Foo::o` by the block
requalifier -- the binder of the eval text saw a GLOBAL: the site never said `$o` is an `our` alias of main.  FIX (Pl + the eval
site): the site hands its in-scope `our` aliases over as pseudo-features `our:CANON=PKG` on the #364 feature channel (the wire
and the cache key unchanged in shape; Binder::ours_visible_at = the innermost visible binding is that `our`; a literal operand
that never spells the name sends none -- _eval_operand_may_name, which now also sees `$#name`); the eval's binder holds them as
outer `our` records; Parser2::_requalify_eval_text spells every non-lexical use homed outside the eval's package qualified.
Probes scratch/s543h/p2/shapes.pl (20 rows: block / single region, @ % and lists, a closed block (control), an inner `my`

write-only, interpolation, the cache with and without the alias, a `package` section of the FILE): tree = perl on 20 (base wrong
on 13); cold / warm / none identical.  Guard eval-capture-01.t our_* (12 rows; 10 fail on the base).  Cost: an eval site gains
`'("our:$o=main" ...)` only for an alias its literal text names (a dynamic operand: every alias in scope) -- counted in the

subject: SILENT WRONG: a caller's `our $o` alias is not seen by a string eval whose text switches package: `our $o = "m"; eval 'sub { package Foo; $o }'` reads $Foo::o, perl reads $main::o (also `eval 'package Foo; $o'`)
triage_reason: string eval name resolution: a caller's `our` alias across a package switch
